  3. Shaders in the browser's own pages (-wren-shader)

#Shaders in the browser's own pages (-wren-shader)

The licence card of about:wren is lit by a real fragment shader reading a real normal map, not by layers of CSS. The toolkit gives Wren an application shader API (gui_toolkit 0.25.0, its docs/shaders.md: render.create_app_shader, draw.app_shader, render.create_texture_data); this page is what Wren builds on it.

#The property

CSS
.base { -wren-shader: card-foil var(--sweep) var(--bx) var(--by) var(--live) 1; }

-wren-shader: none | <name> <argument>*. An argument is a <number>, a <percentage> (its value divided by 100) or a calc() of numbers, at most 28. Not inherited, paint only (a change of the arguments never asks for a layout). The shader fills the box's background painting area (the clip of its bottom background layer, rounded by border-radius) over its CSS background and before its border and its content: what the CSS draws is also what shows when the shader cannot be had.

The arguments are written with var() on purpose. A registered custom property (@property --sweep { syntax: '<number>'; ... }) that a CSS animation moves or a script sets reaches the computed value through the declaration that uses it, and that is what makes the page paint again. A change of the arguments is part of the box's raster signature, so a kept layer holding the box is drawn again when one of them changes and not while they hold still (an animation that rests costs no frame).

#Who may use it

Only the browser's own pages: about:home, about:demos, about:about, about:wren and about:licenses (is_builtin_href, handed to the page by the shell as page.Settings.internal_address; about:blank and every web document are not). In any other document the declaration is invalid (the style engine drops it at computation: Settings.internal_document), so no computed style of a web page ever holds a shader, whatever the cascade, style="" or the CSSOM say. And a name only selects an entry of the registry below: the page supplies numbers and nothing else, never code, a texture or a blend mode. There is no way to bring a shader (no WebGL by the back door).

#The registry (src/browser/shaders.odin)

Each entry declares its WGSL, the Direct3D 11 pixel shader compiled from it (and the SHA-256 of the sources it came from), the names and defaults of its arguments, the textures it reads (made natively, never taken from the page) and its passes (a blend mode each; the box is drawn once per pass). What the shader reads, as vec4 slots (app_param(k)): 0 = the engine's (the box in device pixels, pixels per CSS pixel, 1 when style.prefers_reduced_motion is on), 1 = the pass, then the arguments four to a slot from slot 2.

To add a shader: write src/browser/shaders/<name>.wgsl (the toolkit's frame: fn app_shade(a: AppIn) -> vec4<f32>), run

odin run ext/gui_toolkit/tools/shaders -- app <name> src/browser/shaders/<name>.wgsl src/browser/shaders      # writes <name>.dxbc and <name>.sha256

(naga is built by the toolkit's tools/tk build_naga the first time: it needs cargo), embed the three files and add the entry. The test the_embedded_pixel_shader_matches_its_sources fails while a blob is stale (the sources, or the toolkit's rect.wgsl / app.wgsl, changed): the toolkit refuses such a blob when the shader is created, with a message, and the box keeps its CSS background.

The compositor does not record a box with a shader (its arguments change with every frame of an animation): it is drawn directly, in its place in the paint order, like an image.

#card-foil

Arguments: sweep (0 .. 1: where the sweeping light is on its way across the card; outside, off), pointer-x, pointer-y (0 .. 1: where the pointer is on the card, 0.5 at rest: the tilt the card is given, and the second light), live (0 .. 1: the pointer is on the card: the sweep dims), intensity. Texture 0: the normal map of the card (about_card_relief.odin: R G the normal's x y, B the height, A the cavity). Two passes: Normal (the engraving's shade: the cavities are dark) and Add (the light).

The light pass: for each of two point lights, a Ward anisotropic highlight (brushed foil: long across the brushing, short along it) and an iridescent wash (a thin film: the hue goes round the spectrum with the angle between the normal and the eye, which comes from the tilt); a grid of glitter flakes with a normal each that flash where the light mirrors into the eye, more on the slopes of the engraving; a fresnel rim on the lip of the frame. The result is toned (1 - exp(-x)) so that two lights never burn out the text above.

#The card's turn, and its back (card-back)

Three more arguments after intensity, engrave (1: texture 1 holds the lettering to raise) and the mode seal (0 the card, 1 the seal, 2 the back): rx and ry, the card's turn in degrees (rotateX(rx) rotateY(ry) as the page applies it: the CSS passes var(--rx) var(--ry), registered numbers that transition together with the transform). The eye and the two lights are placed from it in the frame of the face the shader paints (to_face, face_light in card_foil.wgsl): the lights are points of the page over the card's plane, and the face's frame is the card's turned back by rx, ry; the back is the card turned half a turn about the vertical axis (rotateY(180deg) in the page), which mirrors x and z, so that the pointer's light stays where the pointer is on the screen and the back is lit as an object seen from behind. The pointer's own tilt (which used to be derived from pointer-x, pointer-y) is rx = -py * 14, ry = px * 18, written by the page's script.

card-back is the same module in mode 2 with its own textures: texture 0 is the front's relief inside out (about_card_back.odin, relief_map with an emboss field: the height field negated, so the lip is a trough and the furrows of the guilloche ridges; the same grain) with the logo of Wren raised in the middle (the bird of assets/logo_256.png, taken from the light of the picture and its alpha, blurred for the bevel: logo_height_field); texture 1 is a line of raised lettering along the bottom (back_engraving, the brand: WREN · FROMENT SOFTWARE, nothing about the person). Two faces back to back, each backface-visibility: hidden; the one turned away is not painted (open_plane).

#Measured and tested

  • src/style/wren_shader_test.odin: parsing (names, numbers, percentages, calc(), var() and its fallback, the invalid forms), refusal in a document that is not built in (stylesheet, style=""), the arguments following an animated registered property, the end of that animation (a crash before the fix in timeline.odin), paint-only tier.
  • src/browser/shaders_test.odin: the registry, the blob's hash, the normal map (unit normals, deterministic, engraving present, micro-lettering cut), the card's style (no picture in the page), a page painted on WARP (the shader lights its box and only its box, rounded corner, a web page ignores the property, the fallback where the shader is unavailable or unknown, compositor on and off, the arguments move the light).
  • shader_cost (off unless WREN_SHADER_BENCH is set; see the comment above it): the first-use cost and the per-frame cost of the card's two passes on the machine's GPU.
